regime_context: The detector shows a market where AI Infrastructure leads cross-sectional thematics with mediocre durability (0.68) but adequate breadth (0.71), while the rotation view is narrowing (39% eligible) and non-directional — leadership is concentrated but not broadening. The absolute-trend gate IS validated for drawdown control on this market (gate_helps=true), so eligibility is the one leg worth leaning on; everything else is coincident. Crowding is present only in Cybersecurity (z=1.8) and Non-AI Software (z=1.11), which are cautions, not signals. Track record shows direction accuracy near coin-flip (0.483) despite a decent hit rate, so conviction should default low.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Non-AI Tech & Hardware (rank 9, eligible, hurst 'trend', breadth 0.846) continues to hold above eligible status while AI Infrastructure's durability bar slips below 0.60; a confirmed leadership handoff to non-AI hardware would show Non-AI Tech outperforming SMH on a 20-day basis for two consecutive weeks. That observable would retire the watch.

theses.subject: AI Infrastructure
theses.thesis: AI Infrastructure is the rank-1 leader and is trend-gate ELIGIBLE with the broadest quality of the three AI/semi leaders (breadth 0.708 vs Cybersecurity's 1.0 but far more durable cohesion, and with no crowding flag). The legitimate read is not return prediction but staying-power: eligible themes with trend health have historically avoided deeper drawdowns on this market. The detector shows it as the established leader, not a fresh entry; I would lean with the prevailing narrative rather than against it, while noting durability bar of 0.68 is only moderate.
theses.dissent: As the dominant narrative with the highest score, AI Infrastructure is the theme most likely to already reflect attention; the rank-IC on momentum is ~0, so leadership itself gives no forward edge, and durability_bar of 0.68 with hurst_tag 'mixed' means the trend is not cleanly persistent.

falsifier.text: SMH closes below its 50-day simple moving average and AI Infrastructure drops out of eligible status on two consecutive weekly re-ranks before the check-by date.

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is rank-2 and trend-gate eligible with perfect breadth (1.0) and a clean 'trend' hurst tag, but it is the ONLY crowded theme in the top decile (crowding_z=1.8, crowded=true). Per the guardrails, crowding is a size-down caution, never a fade — so this is not a short or underweight; it is an avoid on the long side because the crowding texture signals the theme is late in its attention cycle and chasing it adds reflexivity risk.
theses.dissent: Perfect breadth and a trend hurst tag argue the theme is genuinely healthy and cohesive, and crowding in a confirmed leader can persist for extended periods — avoiding it may mean missing continued upside in a strong-trending theme.

falsifier.text: CIBR outperforms SMH by more than 5% over the next 20 trading days despite the crowding flag.

theses.subject: US Energy Complex
theses.thesis: US Energy Complex is rank-4, eligible, with a clean 'trend' hurst tag and moderate breadth (0.727), and it is the highest-ranked NON-AI/non-tech theme. In a market where the dominant narrative is entirely concentrated in AI/semis, Energy offers a diversification away from the single crowded AI trade while still passing the only validated leg (the absolute-trend gate). This is a diversification lean, not a momentum call.
evidence: category=Energy & Power, distinct from AI concentration
theses.dissent: Energy's momentum score (1.005) is already half that of AI Infrastructure, and it sits on the same trend leg of the market — if the AI complex corrects, a risk-off move could hit Energy's cyclical beta just as hard, offering no true hedge.

falsifier.text: XLE prints a lower low than its prior 20-day low and loses eligible status before the check-by date.
